title: Machine learning on genome-wide cell-free DNA mutation profiles detects lung cancer
summary: Whole-genome sequencing from 2,511 individuals in the Pan-Cancer Analysis of Whole Genomes study and 489 individuals from four prospective cohorts showed region-specific mutation-type frequencies in tissue and cell-free DNA associated with replication timing and chromatin features. A machine-learning model using genome-wide mutational profiles with other features, followed by CT imaging, detected more than 90% of patients with lung cancer, including stage I and II disease. The fixed model was validated in an independent cohort and detected cancer earlier than standard approaches in some patients. The abstract gives limited cohort detail, and this is a detection study, not a deployed screening program.
